minor: "The ads were not paying" is stronger than the listed source. Sergey Brin said in January 2008 that social-network advertising had not worked as well as Google hoped. That is a Google statement, not a Myspace-specific one. Either name Brin's remark or soften the line.
"Had just overtaken" Google rests on one week of Hitwise data (week ending 8 July 2006). Say "in one week" or "by one measure".
"One telling has Timberlake as the public face of a relaunch" is vague. The source only supports that Timberlake took an ownership stake.
The (quote) shot has no actual quotation in its narration. Either use a real quote, such as Brin's line, or change the shot kind.
"Two months later" (IGN), "Eleven months later" (IPO), "barely three years" and "about three years" are derived intervals with no source entries of their own.

Several descriptive claims have no source entry: the Myspace page-building and band-upload features, the glitter and autoplay jumble, and Facebook's plain blue-and-white look. None is wrong, but the Facebook look has no entry.
"Myspace kept the Google deal, and for a while its visitor numbers in America still held up" has no source entry. The comScore April 2008 data supports only that Myspace still led in the US.
"Van Natta's answer was to shrink" is an interpretation of the June 2009 cuts, not a documented motive.
IGN was an agreement to buy in September 2005. "Paid" is fine as shorthand.
